title: Acton teen accused of killing mom, brother ordered held without bail
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Arjun Aravind, 17, was arraigned for the murder of his mother Sudha Venkatesan, 45, and brother Siddharth Aravind, 14.
The victims were found in their Acton home with signs of blunt force trauma, and Aravind was later arrested in Wayland.
Aravind faces charges including murder and motor vehicle theft; he will undergo a mental health evaluation before a Sept. 11 hearing.

title: Downtown Boston was buzzing in July. Here’s a look at the numbers.
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Domestic foot traffic in downtown Boston rose 10.5% in July 2026 compared to July 2025.
Weekend foot traffic reached 104% of 2019 levels, with weekday levels at 75% and increasing steadily.
Events like the World Cup and Sail Boston, plus extended bar hours, boosted downtown economic activity.

title: 2 seriously injured in West End stabbing, police say
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Two people were injured in a suspected domestic stabbing incident in Boston's West End on Thursday morning.
A man and woman were found injured in a building hallway at 55 Causeway St. and taken to a hospital.
The man's injuries were self-inflicted and life-threatening; the woman suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Investigation is ongoing.

title: Healey temporarily restricts kratom sales statewide
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Massachusetts designates kratom as a Schedule I substance, placing new restrictions on its sale statewide for up to a year.
Kratom is linked to serious health risks, including addiction and overdose, prompting the state's emergency order to regulate its sale.
Massachusetts joins other states with kratom restrictions, as officials aim to increase public safety and awareness of its dangers.

title: Two New England beach towns to visit before the summer ends
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich on Cape Cod is a popular destination for its beaches, oyster specials, and sunset cruises.
Chach Restaurant in Provincetown is closing on November 3 after 21 years, as announced by its owners.
Ogunquit, Maine, named New England's best beach town, offers many attractions for day-tripping visitors.

title: Diver dies in incident off Cape Cod
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 72-year-old man died in a diving incident off Cape Cod, near Sesuit Harbor, on Wednesday.
The Dennis Fire Department, along with Marine units and the U.S. Coast Guard, conducted the search operation.
The diver was found and pronounced dead at Sesuit Harbor; the incident is under investigation.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues after graphic testimony about children’s autopsies
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy broke down in court as a medical examiner testified during her ongoing murder trial.
Massachusetts State Police reviewed Clancy's cellphone data, revealing journal entries and Google searches related to mental health.
Testimonies included Clancy's phone and tablet use before the children's deaths, with searches about psychiatric care and suicide methods.

title: Rhode Island beach house with water views on both sides — can you guess the price?
author: Emily Turner
bullets: A beach house in Westerly, Rhode Island offers water views on both sides.
The 2,724 square foot house features 3 bedrooms and 3 full baths, built in 1987.
Property taxes for 2025 are $11,125, with potential listing prices ranging from $1.78 to $1.98 million.

title: 5 best new restaurant openings and dining updates in Boston (August 13, 2026)
author: Nathan Tavares
bullets: First Crush, a natural wine bar by Gabrielle Malina, opens in Somerville's Union Square in mid-September 2026.
Chef Jeff Almendras turns his Filipino-inspired popup into a permanent restaurant, Johnny Boy, in Fort Point this fall.
Tiffani Faison's new office-themed bar, The Temp Agency, is now open at High Street Place in Downtown Boston.

title: 3 concerning trends from Red Sox’ 5-game losing skid
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox suffer five-game losing streak, scoring only 2.8 runs per game, down from a previous average of 5.6.
Bullpen shows signs of strain; Tyron Guerrero and Aroldis Chapman struggle, while Garrett Whitlock faces potential IL stint.
Defensive errors, such as Willson Contreras's dropped ball, contribute to recent Red Sox losses and performance decline.
